decisions.executionNote: Begin a small elbow-up approach toward the left end of the set square; keep the right arm at reset.
Use closed fingertips behind the straightedge, rather than lifting blocks. Lower both arms in small continuous increments toward its two ends.
Continue lowering behind the bar, correcting slight wrist pitch drift; two separated contact points will let the bar square up without grasping cubes.
Advance slightly while lowering, using smaller wrist corrections and continuous elbow-up targets. Still clear of the straightedge.
Reduce approach increments after the continuity rejection; replan from the unchanged observation.
Pitch the closed fingers gently downward while approaching the bar height; keep both contacts outside the cubes.
Bring fingertip heights close to the tabletop behind the straightedge, with the right contact moved inward to its endpoint.
Place closed fingertips behind—not over—the straightedge before contact. Move the right fingertip within the bar's span.
Lower only the fingertip contact region through gentle downward pitch while keeping elbow-up continuity. Watch for the bar to move before any block contact.
Finish a shallow tabletop approach, keeping the two closed finger tips behind the angled bar. The blocks remain untouched.
Hold the left contact steady and lower the right fingertip toward the bar's rear face. Prepare to advance the right end first to make the edge horizontal.
The right finger appears over the bar rather than behind it. Lift it clear and back off slightly before a side-contact approach; leave cubes undisturbed.
Set the right contact just behind the bar at a lower height, using millimeter-scale increments and leaving the left contact still.
Gently push the bar's right end forward while the left end stays supported, reducing the bar's yaw before aligning the cubes.
The initial right advance passed over the edge without translating it. Back off and lower the right contact 2 cm for a true side push.
Push forward again at the corrected right fingertip height, monitoring the straightedge rather than assuming contact from arm tracking.
Confirmed the right end is translating along the table. Continue squaring the long edge with the left endpoint held in place.
Remove the remaining small straightedge angle with a 2 cm right-end advance before pushing both ends together.
The straightedge is now horizontal. Advance both ends together along the tabletop to collect the staggered cubes into one row, without lifting.
Two cubes have reached the edge; the third is still slightly ahead. Continue gently, with a small left-end correction to keep the resulting row level.
All three cubes now appear level against the straightedge. Withdraw both fingers backward and upward without disturbing the row, beginning the reset.
Open the now-clear grippers and return toward the initial separated wrist positions, progressively restoring the original wrist orientation.
